## SECTION 0 — EXECUTIVE SUMMARY, DATA HYGIENE & HOW TO WEIGHT THIS PACK

### 0.1 Verdict up front

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Current price (2026-08-24) | $87.85 |
| Probability-weighted intrinsic value | **$43.2/share** |
| Bear / Base / Bull cases | $28.1 / $43.6 / $64.6 |
| Implied upside from today | **−51%** |
| Margin of safety vs. 30% requirement | **FAIL** (price is 2.0× intrinsic value) |
| Max buy price for 30% MoS | ≈ $30 |
| Action | **Do not initiate. If held, sell/reduce.** |

The market is paying $87.85 for a company whose guided 2026 earnings (~$2.00 GAAP/share) put it at ~44× forward GAAP EPS. My base-case DCF — which *pays the company credit for the entire 6,400-channel replacement cycle, a 27–29% structural net margin, and a rich single-product niche moat* — still only supports ~$44. Even my bull case (European CE clearance lands, international opens, greenfield wins, margin holds at 29–30%) reaches only $65. For the market price to be fair, you must assume either a fundamentally lower discount rate (~6%, i.e., almost no equity risk premium over 10-year Treasuries for a $1.1B single-product micro-cap) **or** FCF growth beyond the replacement cycle that no filed filing, call, or guide supports.

### 0.2 Data-pack hygiene — what I flagged before using

1. **Series continuity:** Revenue step FY2015→FY2016 (~$32M→$32M, no step) and FY2017 dip (−28%) and FY2020 dip (−18%, COVID) are real business events, not basis changes. No XBRL basis step >20% unexplained. Checked. [Arithmetic]
2. **Capex discontinuity:** TTM capex ($0.002B) vs FY2025 capex ($0.008B) — explained by the $20M facility build-out (Orlando, [Estimate], web research) occurring mostly in 2025. TTM capex is a trailing-smoothing artifact, not a basis change.
3. **Vendor cash $0.051B (Section 2) vs balance-sheet cash (Section 6, FY2025 $0.051B)** — consistent; T0 cash is actually $59.1M per the Q2 2026 10-Q (company call). I use $59.1M.
4. **Long-term debt = none; vendor total debt = $0** — consistent. Net cash is the entire $59.1M.
5. **Marketable securities:** Pack explicitly says NOT EXTRACTED. Confirmed via 10-Q snippet: "Our treasury bills are included as Cash and Cash Equivalents…" — so marketable securities are de minimis. No adjustment needed.
6. **Weighted-average shares 12.854M (FY25), not split-adjusted; no split suspected.** Use ~12.9–13.0M for 2026–2035 modeling.
7. **Beta (0.91) window unstated** — treated as an [Estimate] only; I derive the discount rate with multiple sensitivity points.

### 0.3 Sourcing convention used throughout this report

- **[Actual]** = company filed/company statement (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, earnings call management speech)
- **[Estimate]** = third-party aggregator, analyst, or vendor
- **[Assumption]** = my own judgment, disclosed and not silently buried

**Business model:** IRMD designs and sells the **only FDA-cleared true MRI-compatible IV infusion pump systems** (MRidium 3860+/3861 and the newly launched 3870), plus MRI-compatible patient monitors, ferro-magnetic detection systems, and proprietary disposables. The disposables attach to an installed base and create recurring, high-margin (76.7% [Estimate]) revenue.

**Moat:** The barrier is regulatory (FDA 510(k), EU CE marking) plus 20+ years of installed-base lock-in. The company's own claim — "[we are] recognized as the only true MRI compatible IV infusion pumps on the market" [Estimate, csimarket] — is consistent with all sources I found; no direct competitor names appear anywhere in web research. That gives pricing power. The counterweight: it is a **single-product-category niche**, dependent on MRI suite capital budgets, and conventional pump giants (Baxter, ICU Medical, B. Braun) could eventually enter with FDA submissions. Margin of safety must reflect that asymmetry.

## SECTION 5 — DISCOUNT RATE DERIVATION (CAPM → WACC)

**Capital structure:** 100% equity. $59.1M cash, $0 debt. No operating leases of any size (pack Section 6B shows ~$0–3M, immaterial). Therefore WACC = cost of equity.

### 5.1 Components

| Component | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Risk-free rate | 4.69% | 10-yr UST, 2026-08-20 (FRED DGS10) [Actual—market] |
| Equity risk premium | 4.4% | Damodaran-style long-run implied ERP [Assumption] |
| Beta | 0.91 | Vendor ([Estimate], window unstated) |
| CAPM cost of equity | 4.69% + 0.91 × 4.4% = **8.7%** | [Arithmetic] |
| Size/illiquidity premium | +0.8% | Market cap $1.1B; thin liquidity; single-product concentration [Assumption] |
| **Applied cost of equity (base)** | **9.5%** | Rounds up for key-person reliance (CEO Susi; founder-led culture) |

### 5.2 Why not lower?

A 6% cost of equity — which is what the current share price implies on my base-case cash flows — would demand almost no risk premium over a 4.69% risk-free rate for a company whose product roadmap is one FDA-cleared niche pump, whose production is scaling 130→300+ units in a single quarter, whose revenue growth just printed +0.5%, and whose international approvals are still pending. That makes no sense. 8.0% is the absolute floor I would use for a best-case blue-sky scenario; my base sits at 9.5%.

- **2027–2029:** Anchored to management's explicit replacement-cycle target: **6,400 old 3860/3861 channels** at least five years old; management targets **~1,000 channels/year**; quad mix 70%; quad ASP **$110K** (⇒ ~$27.5K/channel). [Actual, Q2'26 call + TipRanks]. That implies ~$14–16M/year of pump-driven growth in 2027–2028 plus disposables (+14%), monitors (+12%), FMD (+57%). My base uses +15.5% (2027), +12% (2028), +9% (2029) — this delivers roughly 70% of the full replacement value by 2030, acknowledging ramp and mix frictions. **This is a full-capture-of-the-visible-cycle assumption, not conservative.**
- **2030–2035:** Fade toward terminal ~3%. The MRI-compatible pump market is modeled at 8.3–12.3% CAGR through 2031 [Estimate]; my 2030 (~6.8%) and converging-to-3% path is a rational premium-to-rental-fade for a niche leader. Beyond 2033 there is **no guided source** — this is [Assumption] and is deliberately tested in bull/bear.

**Margins:**
- 2026: 27.0% net margin. Derivation: GAAP EPS guide ≈ $1.89–2.04 (non-GAAP $2.09–2.24 [Actual] minus ~$0.20 SBC/share [Arithmetic on pack SBC series]); NI ≈ $24.4–26.3M; mid ≈ $25.2M.
- 2027–2029: 28.5–29.0% net margin — GM recovers from 74% back to 76–77% as startup costs drop >50% in Q3 [Actual]; opex (Q2'26: −4% y/y) deleverages on volume.
- 2030–2035: fade from 28.5% → 26.0% as competition and scale costs creep; this is [Assumption].

**Capex / D&A / WC:**
- 2026: capex ~$5M (facility tail; TTM shows only $2M spent so far, capacity expansion for 300+ units/quarter needs modest tooling) [Assumption]; D&A rises to ~$1.5M on higher PP&E base [Arithmetic on net PP&E growth].
- 2027–2035: capex ~4% of revenue (declining to 3%); D&A converges up to ~3% of revenue [Assumption].
- ΔWC: ~15% of annual revenue growth (reflecting 19% non-cash WC ratio, slightly disciplined) [Assumption].

**FCFE definition:** NI − capex + D&A − ΔWC (100% equity; no debt; GAAP NI already deducts SBC). This is the correct equity-cash-flow treatment for an unlevered, SBC-paying firm. The pack's instruction that SBC must be deducted is honored automatically because I model GAAP net income.
